proposition.claim:
The operative genericity condition is Definition 4.9, PDF p. 40: \(\prod_i\det C_i=1\), and for every \(1\le r<n\), every choice of \(r\) eigenvalues from each \(C_i\) has total product different from one. A common invariant proper subspace would violate this condition by taking determinants on that subspace. It therefore excludes reducible representations, rather than merely imposing a condition on the full determinant. The introductory omission of \(r=1\), and the repeated subscript in the determinant product, are resolved by the body definition and are not additional Problems.

The smoothness and scalar-stabilizer interface in Theorem 4.10 agrees with the explicitly consulted author version of Hausel–Letellier–Rodriguez-Villegas [hlrv], Definition 2.1.1, Proposition 2.1.4 and Theorem 2.1.5, PDF pp. 16–18. Nonemptiness is kept separate from smoothness of a possibly empty variety. At \(k=0\), the genericity condition excludes \(n>1\); when \(n=1\), the resulting space is \((\mathbb C^*)^{2g}\). Thus Theorem 8.13 does not assert an unrestricted result for all untwisted higher-rank character varieties.

Equation reference: eq:middle. For a regular semisimple last puncture, set \(r=\binom n2\) and \(d=\dim_{\mathbb C}X\). Theorem 1.2 gives a rank-\(r\) vector bundle over \(X\), with strata \[(\mathbb C^*)^{d-2i}\times\mathbb C^{i+r}.\] The center of the compact-support curious Lefschetz symmetry on each stratum is \[
 (d-2i)+2(i+r)=d+2r.\] The affine-bundle isomorphism shifts cohomological degree and weight by \(2r\), recovering center \(d\) for \(X\). Consequently Proposition 2.19 is applied with a common center on all strata. The long exact compact-support sequence is compatible with cup product, and strictness of mixed Hodge structures makes its weight-graded rows exact. The five-lemma argument then preserves the asserted isomorphisms.

Equation reference: eq:inversion, eq:printed. Write \(N=\cup\omega\), assume that \(X\) is Tate, \(\omega\in F^2H^2(X)\), and \(N\) satisfies curious Lefschetz with middle weight \(2d\). The proposition defines \[g_a(u)=\sum_k u^k\dim\ker\bigl(N^a:H_c^k(X)\longrightarrow
 H_c^{k+2a}(X)\bigr)\quad(a>0),\qquad g_a=0\quad(a\le0),\] and \[
 f_i(u)=(1+u^2)g_{i+1}(u)-g_i(u)-u^2g_{i+2}(u).\] Its claimed output is \[
 \operatorname{MH}_X(u,v)=\sum_{i\ge0}v^{d-i}f_i(u)
       \frac{(uv)^{i+1}-1}{uv-1},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{MH}_X(u,v)=\sum_{k,j}u^kv^j\dim H_c^k(X)^{j,j}.\] The quotient is a finite polynomial sum, so the issue is unrelated to substitution at \(uv=1\).

X=(C*)² smooth Tate,ω=dlogx∧dlogy inF²H² nonzero; Hc²=C(0),Hc³=C(-1)^2,Hc4=C(-2); cupωHc²→Hc4 isomorphism byPoincare duality;CHLmiddle2,d1.
